description: Is service setup fast and healthy right now, and if not, why: slow versus stalled setups, where setup time goes, API latency versus client throttling, and the leader changes and restarts behind outliers.

panels.description: Request acceptance to first successful SetupComplete for completions in the selected range. -1 means the telemetry is not deployed or no successful setup exists in the range.
panels.title: User setup p95

panels.description: Authorization to first successful SetupComplete for completions in the selected range. External approval time is excluded. -1 means no observation is available.
panels.title: Platform setup p95

panels.description: Successful initial setup attempts in the selected dashboard range. Zero is valid only while observer telemetry is present.
panels.title: Completed setups

panels.description: Unfinished setups between one minute and one hour past authorization: work that should finish but has not yet. This is the number to act on. Stalled setups are counted separately. Releases without the stalled gauge count every overdue setup here.

targets.expr: ((sum(service_catalog_setup_overdue) - (sum(service_catalog_setup_stalled) or vector(0))) and on() (max(service_catalog_setup_observer_healthy) == 1)) or ((max(service_catalog_setup_observer_healthy) == 1) * 0) or ((max(service_catalog_setup_observer_healthy) == 0) - 1) or (absent(service_catalog_setup_observer_healthy) * -1)

panels.title: Slow right now

panels.description: Unfinished setups more than an hour past authorization. These wait on a known blocker, not on controller speed; see Stalled setups by blocking stage for what each one needs. Telemetry unavailable means setups are unfinished but the deployed release does not report which are stalled.

targets.expr: (absent(service_catalog_setup_stalled) * -1 and on() count(service_catalog_setup_inflight)) or (((sum(service_catalog_setup_stalled)) and on() (max(service_catalog_setup_observer_healthy) == 1)) or ((max(service_catalog_setup_observer_healthy) == 1) * 0) or ((max(service_catalog_setup_observer_healthy) == 0) - 1) or (absent(service_catalog_setup_observer_healthy) * -1))

panels.title: Stalled (>1h)

panels.description: Whether all source caches needed to interpret setup state are synchronized on the projection owner. The unfinished-work numbers are trustworthy only while this is Healthy.
panels.title: Setup observer

panels.description: End-to-end p95. The -1 fallback keeps the panel explicit before telemetry rollout or during an idle range; use Setup observer before interpreting it. Annotations mark controller starts and leader acquisitions, which cause most outliers.

targets.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service_class, clock) (rate(service_catalog_setup_duration_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))) or (label_replace(label_replace(absent(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service_class, clock) (rate(service_catalog_setup_duration_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))) * -1, "service_class", "none", "", ""), "clock", "no observations", "", ""))

panels.title: Setup latency by service class and clock

panels.description: Setups still unfinished more than an hour after authorization. Retrying does not fix these: they wait on configuration such as a service with no available locations or provider resources that cannot be installed. Each row is a service class and the first incomplete setup stage, with the age of its oldest attempt. Empty also while the setup observer is unhealthy; check Setup observer first. Telemetry unavailable means setups are unfinished but the deployed release does not report which are stalled.

Authorization.text: Authorization: access not approved, or project suspended

Dependencies.text: Dependencies: a required service has not finished setup

Projection.text: Projection: no available locations, or availability not converged

Provisioning.text: Provisioning: provider resources not installed (see the Provisioned condition)

max by (service_class, blocking_stage) (service_catalog_setup_oldest_inflight_seconds and on(service_class, operation, blocking_stage) (service_catalog_setup_stalled > 0)) and on() (max(service_catalog_setup_observer_healthy) == 1)

The legend reports only the range maximum because a disappeared stage has no trustworthy current sample. -1 means coverage is unavailable; a healthy empty observer reports zero.

panels.description: Time a request waits in each setup controller queue before a worker picks it up. High wait with normal reconcile time means too little worker capacity or a backlog after a restart.
panels.title: Queue wait p95 by controller

panels.description: Time each setup controller spends on one reconcile after dequeue. Rising reconcile time with normal queue wait points at slow Kubernetes API calls or client throttling; see the API section below.
panels.title: Reconcile time p95 by controller

panels.description: Reconciles that returned an error and will retry with backoff. Each retry adds backoff delay to setup.
panels.title: Reconcile errors by controller

panels.description: Reconciles that asked to run again, either immediately (requeue) or after a delay (requeue_after). Sustained requeues usually mean a controller is waiting on another stage.
panels.title: Requeues by controller

panels.description: Requests waiting for a worker in each setup controller queue.
panels.title: Queue depth by controller

panels.description: Execution time for bounded projection phases inside a location-projection reconcile. This does not include workqueue delay.

targets.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, phase) (rate(service_catalog_projection_phase_duration_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))) or label_replace(absent(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, phase) (rate(service_catalog_projection_phase_duration_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))) * -1, "phase", "no observations", "", "")

panels.title: Projection phase p95

panels.description: Successful setup attempts per interval and service class. Each completion is counted once. Zero means no completion was recorded; observer health shows whether coverage is trustworthy.
panels.title: Setup completion volume by class
Kubernetes API: slow server or client throttling?

panels.description: Sustained requests per second (qps) and burst size each of the controller's API clients may send before client-go makes it wait (one client per resource kind per project). A limit near the request rate below caps setup speed; client-go defaults to 5 qps with a burst of 10 when nothing sets a limit. No client limit leaves throttling to the API server.
panels.title: Client rate limit

panels.description: Controller-wide Kubernetes API round-trip latency, excluding time waiting on the client rate limiter. High values mean the API servers are slow. Not exported yet means the deployed release does not register client-go latency metrics.
panels.title: API round-trip p95

panels.description: Controller-wide time requests wait for a client-side rate-limit token before being sent. High values mean the controller is throttling itself, not that the API is slow. No client limit means requests never wait here. Not exported yet must not be read as zero wait.

targets.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(rest_client_rate_limiter_duration_seconds_bucket{job="services-system/services-controller-manager"}[$__rate_interval])))) or ((max(service_catalog_client_rate_limit{job="services-system/services-controller-manager",limit="qps"}) == 0) - 2) or ((sum(absent(rest_client_rate_limiter_duration_seconds_bucket{job="services-system/services-controller-manager"})) * -1) and on() absent(service_catalog_client_rate_limit{job="services-system/services-controller-manager",limit="qps"}))

panels.title: Client throttle wait p95

panels.description: Share of total request time spent waiting on the client rate limiter rather than on the API server. Above roughly 10% the controller limits itself; below it, slowness comes from the server.
panels.title: Request time spent throttled

panels.description: Kubernetes API responses rejected by server-side throttling (API priority and fairness). client-go retries these after the server's Retry-After delay; see Throttled and retried requests by verb.
panels.title: HTTP 429 rate

panels.description: Controller-wide p95 API round-trip latency by scope (root is the platform API, project is any project control plane) and HTTP verb. Client metrics have no reconciler label; compare with Reconcile time p95 by controller.

defaults.noValue: No requests in range, or client-go latency metrics not exported yet

panels.title: API round-trip p95 by verb and scope

panels.description: Controller-wide p95 wait for a client-side rate-limit token by scope (root is the platform API, project is any project control plane) and HTTP verb. Empty when Client rate limit shows No client limit, because requests then never wait on the client.

defaults.noValue: No requests in range, no client limit, or client-go rate-limiter metrics not exported yet

panels.title: Client throttle wait p95 by verb and scope

panels.description: Controller-wide REST traffic grouped by HTTP response code.
panels.title: Kubernetes API request rate by response code

panels.description: Responses the API server throttled (HTTP 429, counted per attempt) and the retry attempts client-go made, by HTTP verb. A retry's code is what that retry attempt returned, not what triggered it: 200 means the retry succeeded, and a 429 retry means the server throttled it again. Each retry waits for the Retry-After delay, so sustained 429s slow setup even with no client limit.

defaults.noValue: No 429 responses or client retries in range

panels.title: Throttled and retried requests by verb

panels.description: Times a replica acquired a manager lease in the selected range, across the primary and projection elections. Each change stalls that manager while the new leader starts, syncs caches and reconnects projects.
panels.title: Leader changes

panels.description: Controller processes started in the selected range: new pods from rollouts plus in-place container restarts from crashes and leadership-loss exits. Setup right after a start waits for projects to reconnect.
panels.title: Controller starts

panels.description: Container restarts in place during the selected range. Leadership loss intentionally terminates the process, so restarts usually pair with a leader change.
panels.title: Container restarts

panels.description: Project control planes queued for connection. Every project is queued after a start or failover; setup in a project waits until it is reconnected. Should return to zero within seconds.
panels.title: Projects awaiting reconnection

panels.description: Exactly one replica should own the projection lease. -1 means this release has not exposed the distinct projection election.
panels.title: Projection leaders

panels.description: Exactly one primary controller manager leader is expected.
panels.title: Primary manager leaders

panels.description: Projects still waiting to be reconnected on each replica. After a start the backlog jumps to every project and drains; the time to drain is the time to reconnect projects after a restart.
panels.title: Project reconnection backlog by replica

panels.description: Which replica holds each manager lease. A line ending and another starting is a leader change.
panels.title: Lease holder by manager

panels.description: Seconds since the aggregate writer last completed a successful observation pass. -1 means it has never reported.
